subject: Runtime retry behavior causing doubled token counts for Stratus Health demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo failure: automatic retry seems to be doubling token usage (Stratus Health)

Hi team,

Quick heads-up from today's demo with Stratus Health (Taylor Green). During a short upstream hiccup the client SDK retried a generation request and the customer saw a doubled token count and a repeated paragraph in the output. They flagged potential billing impact and confusion for end users.

What I have:
- Repro steps (attached repro_script.sh) that we used in the demo environment
- Logs from their session (logs_20270520.txt)
- HubSpot deal: SH-2027-0412 (link below)

Immediate asks:
1) Can Platform/Runtime triage whether this looks like an SDK retry + runtime fallback interaction (is there a case where a retry produces a new full generation instead of resuming)?
2) Is there a short-term config we can flip (server-side or account-level) to prevent duplicate billing for this customer while we investigate?
3) ETA on a fix or mitigation we can communicate to Taylor today — they are scoped for a POC and procurement is watching cost behavior closely.

I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: logs_20270520.txt, repro_script.sh, screenshot_error.png

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo failure: automatic retry seems to be doubling token usage (Stratus Health)

Thanks for the report, Marissa — I skimmed the logs and repro steps you attached. A couple quick notes:

- The SDK is configured to retry on transport errors by default. Retries send the same payload unless the client generates a new request idempotency key.
- I see from the logs that the original request did not complete (timeout on token stream) and we then served a fallback variant on the next attempt. If the runtime treats the fallback as a distinct invocation, token accounting could show both generations.

Can you confirm the exact sequence you used in the repro (we want the exact CLI/API calls)? If you can paste the repro command output (stdout/stderr) it will help.

Short-term mitigation options we can consider today:
- Disable client-side retries for this account (quick, but requires coordination with SDK owners and the customer).
- Apply a server-side dedupe window keyed by request-id (this requires a small change in the API layer; I can prototype but not immediate).

I will try to reproduce locally once I have the exact steps. If this is in the POC environment we can also toggle account-level retry=false for Stratus Health to buy time.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo failure: automatic retry seems to be doubling token usage (Stratus Health)

Thanks Dev — repro steps below (copied from the script we ran against their staging key):

1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <staging-key>" -d '{"prompt":"Summarize patient intake triage","max_tokens":256}' --connect-timeout 3 --retry 2
2) Simulate network pause for ~2s (we did this via traffic shaping in their demo environment).
3) Client observed timeout and retried; final output contained the summary twice.

Logs excerpts in logs_20270520.txt show two separate generation events with distinct request ids, but identical prompt and token counts. HubSpot notes: customer is sensitive to per-token billing during POC.

I can disable client retries on the demo key if that helps short-term. Prefer something server-side if possible so we don't rely on the customer changing config.

Taylor (cc'd in the original report) — sorry for the noise today. We're treating this as high priority and will get back with a recommended mitigation.

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo failure: automatic retry seems to be doubling token usage (Stratus Health)

I dug into the runtime traces and this looks like an interaction between fallback variant routing and prefix/KV cache invalidation. High-level:

- When a request times out on the token stream we currently allow the SDK to retry as a fresh invocation.
- The runtime chooses a fallback variant (smaller model) if the original backend is overloaded or unavailable. Unfortunately, the KV-prefix cache is not always applied across variant boundaries if the cache entry was created on the original backend and not shared; the retry ends up being treated as a separate full generation.

Root cause hypothesis: retries are producing distinct request ids and the API layer does not enforce a short dedupe window keyed by a client-provided idempotency key. Combined with variant routing and non-shared KV cache, this yields two full generations and double token accounting.

Recommended next steps (order-of-operations):
1) Emergency short-term: enable account-level flag to disable client retries for Stratus Health POC and mark for billing protection. Marissa — please confirm if you want us to flip this now; it can be reverted.
2) Short-term server-side mitigation (48–72 hrs): implement a 30s dedupe window at the API gateway keyed by X-Request-Id or client-provided idempotency-key to collapse retries into a single accounting event. This will cover most retry storms without changing SDKs.
3) Medium-term (2–4 weeks): ensure KV-prefix cache cross-variant consistency or carry prefix cache state during retry attempts so fallback invocations can resume rather than re-generate.

I'll open INFRA-1298 with the proposed patch for the API dedupe; Dev, can you spike the prototype for the gateway change? If we can get a small patch through we can communicate a fix to Taylor by EOD tomorrow.

Also: add a line in the POC onboarding doc advising customers to disable aggressive client retries for short-lived demos until we deploy the dedupe window.

—Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Runtime
